General situation: Over the past 30 days, global grains and oilseeds markets have shown mixed but stable dynamics with no significant bullish or bearish shifts. Bunge’s soybean crush margins are under pressure as soybean input prices rise faster than soy oil and meal outputs, compressing margins despite a rich valuation and high post-merger debt. Black Sea wheat prices have increased by 5-7% compared to the previous month, supported by freight parity enabling exports to ASEAN countries. Brazilian soybean export offers to China remain limited due to freight and phytosanitary certification risks, although Chinese crushers maintain healthy crush margins and improving soybean meal sales. What changed vs previous comparable period: This month saw an emergence of three key market signals compared to none in the prior month, reflecting increased market commentary but no directional price impact. Black Sea wheat prices have firmed relative to last month, while Brazilian soybean export availability tightened, contrasting with previously more fluid offers. Actionable implications for trading/brokerage: Traders should monitor Bunge’s margin squeeze risk amid rising soybean prices and uncertain biofuel tax credits, which may pressure spreads. The firming Black Sea wheat prices and freight parity open export opportunities to ASEAN markets, suggesting potential for increased trade flows. Limited Brazilian soybean offers to China warrant caution on supply availability and freight risk premiums. Broker desk offers for April corn CIF at 241 EUR and bids for early March sunflower at 301 USD indicate active price discovery in these segments. 

Key facts:
- Bunge’s EV/EBITDA at 10x, highest in sector, with $12.2B post-Viterra merger debt as of March 18, 2026.
- Black Sea wheat FOB prices inflated by 5-7% since February 2026, supporting exports to ASEAN.
- INR/USD exchange rate steady at 93/94, with Chicago USDA wheat prices above $600 per unit.
- Brazilian soybean export offers to China limited in early March 2026 due to freight and phytosanitary risks.
- Broker desk reports corn CIF offers at 241 EUR for April 10-30 delivery and sunflower CPT bids at 301 USD for early March.
- Chinese crushers maintain good crush margins and improving soybean meal sales despite supply-side constraints.
